Before Bun 1.5, `.resolves`, `.rejects` and `toThrow()` of an async function blocked until the promise settled. Now they return a promise, as in Jest and Vitest, so the code after an assertion that isn't awaited runs first.

`--fix` adds `await` and makes the function `async`. If that function is a helper, it awaits the calls to it in the same file, and it turns a `forEach` over an array into `for..of`. It changes nothing if the test still wouldn't wait, as in an exported helper or an event listener, or if waiting can change the result, as in a test that calls `done` later.

The rule checks files that import from `bun:test`, `vitest` or `@jest/globals`, and files that use the globals.

`bun lint --upgrade` runs this rule. See [Upgrade Bun](/lint#upgrade-bun).

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"bun/await-async-expect" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```ts
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";

test("saves the user", () => {
  expect(save(user)).resolves.toBe(true);
  expect(async () => save(null)).toThrow("no user");
  expect(saved()).toEqual([user]);
});
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";

test("saves the user", async () => {
  await expect(save(user)).resolves.toBe(true);
  await expect(async () => save(null)).toThrow("no user");
  expect(saved()).toEqual([user]);
});

test("rejects an unknown id", () => {
  return expect(load(-1)).rejects.toThrow("not found");
});
```
